I gave up eating meat when I was a teenager, it wasn't hard, I didn't do it for the animals I just couldn't stand the chewing process. Fast forward 20 years and my boyfriend persuaded me to try a piece of steak, 'It will melt in your mouth.' he told me. He was right, it did and it tasted great. Turns out my mum was just a really, really bad cook! My new lease of life as a carnivore started taking shape, sausages, bacon, sausages in bacon...I ate it all. Then along came Social Media. It turned out I knew too many vegetarians and Vegans on Facebook, the videos just kept coming and coming, pigs, cows, sheep, all sad and not wanting to die. After one particularly disturbing piggy video, I put down my knife and fork and started grazing on some salad leaves. I was back to being a proper vegetarian, it was fine, I'd done it before and I could do it again, any temptation soon evaporated when I thought of that poor little piggy. But then the Vgang upped their game, it all became about dairy, baby calves being taken from their mothers, dairy cows crying as they were taken away. It all became too much and I took the step and became a vegan. Being a vegan is very hard, no matter what the plant-based eating brigade tell you. The worst thing about finding some vegan edibles was to then discover they contain palm oil, right at the time everyone was up in arms about palm oil. I could no longer go food shopping without my glasses and a list of meat, fish, eggs, dairy, palm oil free products. I didn't have to worry too much about plastic packaging or buying plastic bags as I had nothing to put in them anyway. I didn't eat vegan cheese despite being a big cheese eater, because it is disgusting. So after two weeks dairy free I imploded and ordered the cheesiest pizza on the menu. This is what happens when you deprive yourself of something you enjoy, you binge on it when you fall off the wagon. So I started eating cheese again but stuck to the other changes. THEN it became about my make-up, was it cruelty-free? My clothes, shoes, bedding, towels, curtains, cushion covers, china, cutlery pretty much anything you come into contact in daily life. Who made it? What conditions do they work in? How old are they? How much do they get paid? Ultimately I learned the only way I could save the animals, save the children, and save the planet would be to lay naked in a field in the middle of nowhere and eat nothing! Comments
